meta.keyPoints: Hospital Portfolio[1] [2] The company is a healthcare service provider in India, operating a network of 55 healthcare facilities across India, along with a presence in the Cayman Islands and the UK. The company owns and operates certain hospitals, while others are operated under management agreements, under which Narayana Health acquires operating control of the facilities.

assumptions._note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Narayana Hrudayalaya (consolidated, ₹ crore). Segment model on the businesses the company reports: India hospitals, Cayman hospitals, UK (Practice Plus Group, consolidated from 6-Nov-2025), Cayman insurance (CIHL), India clinics + India insurance (NHIC + NHIL, reported together), and an eliminations line (zero margin). Segment split follows PL's reading of the company's disclosures (see segments.json). EBITDA is post-Ind AS 116 (Screener basis); lease liabilities (₹991 cr at Mar-26, mostly UK) sit in borrowings, so the model's net debt includes them. FX held at the Q1FY27 averages implied by the deck and PL (₹94.7/US$, ₹127/GBP). Shares: Screener's FY26 Net Profit ÷ EPS gives 20.45 cr, matching the 20.44 cr shares outstanding (20,43,60,804, incl. 12.6 lakh held by the ESOP trust), so no patch is needed; minorities are ~₹0.4 cr a year. Valued on a sum of the parts (EV/EBITDA by segment on Sep-28E), as the street does.

segments.name: India hospitals
segments._why: Bed build (businessLines.india): occupied beds × ARPOB (₹ mn per occupied bed a year, the company's measure) less ~₹66 cr of revenue the company's India-hospital figure carries but consolidation eliminates (PL split; FY26 ₹69 cr, Q1FY27 ₹16.5 cr). FY26: ₹4,740 cr = ~2,648 occupied beds × ₹17.9 mn. FY27E: 2,780 occupied beds (+5%: IP discharges +8% and OP +9% YoY in Q1FY27 with no new beds; South-West Bengaluru, 100 leased beds, opens end-Q2FY27) × ₹19.4 mn (+8%; Q1FY27 ₹19.2 mn, +9% YoY on case mix, robotics and ALOS falling from 4.3 toward 3.9-4.0 days; list-price increases are 'low to mid single digits'). FY28E: 2,900 × ₹20.6 mn (HSR 215 beds and Raipur 300 beds complete in FY28, so little revenue that year). FY29E: 3,080 × ₹21.7 mn (HSR and Raipur ramping; Rajarhat and Central Bengaluru pushed to FY29, South Bengaluru to FY30 in the Q1FY27 deck). Revenue +14% / +11% / +12% (FY26 +10%, Q1FY27 +16%).
segments._marginWhy: PL-basis EBITDA margin 19.3% (FY25), 21.8% (FY26), 23.2% (Q1FY27; company basis 24.8%, which includes the eliminated income). No beds were added for 7-8 quarters, so ARPOB growth fell through to margin (+400bp YoY in Q1). Management expects core margin expansion to continue but says new-centre losses start from late FY27 (South-West Bengaluru) and FY28 (HSR, Raipur). We hold 23.5% for FY27-28E and trim to 23.0% in FY29E as two new hospitals carry start-up losses. Each 1pp is ~₹59 cr of FY28E EBITDA (~₹2.3 of EPS).

segments.name: Cayman hospitals
segments._why: Health City Cayman Islands (East End) and Health City Camana Bay, 164 operational beds. Hospital revenue net of insurance eliminations: US$172.1 mn in FY26 (US$178.7 mn less US$6.6 mn), +27% on the Camana Bay ramp and steerage from the group's own insurer. Q1FY27 US$42.8 mn net, +5% YoY (seasonally weak; discharges +6%, OP +12%; July-August 'improved'). Management: double-digit growth 'not physically possible' to sustain; growth will come from the insurer and other Caribbean islands. US$185.9 / 198.9 / 210.8 mn (+8% / +7% / +6%) at ₹94.7 (FY26 average ~₹88.3, so FY27E ₹ growth +16%). No new Cayman capex is planned.
segments._marginWhy: PL-basis margin 42.7% (FY25), 45.6% (FY26), 41.3% (Q1FY27, the seasonal low; 43.7% in Q1FY26). PL's split puts the eliminated income in Cayman; on the company's own India figure the Cayman hospital margin is ~39%. Management: hospital margin 'preserved' through the Camana Bay expansion. 44% / 44.5% / 44.5%.

segments.name: UK (Practice Plus Group)
segments._why: 13 facilities, 330 beds, 37 theatres, ~95% NHS-funded at acquisition. FY26 holds five months (£110 mn). Pre-deal revenue £229 mn (FY24, Sep year-end) and £250 mn (FY25E), 12% CAGR over five years; Q1FY27 £65.0 mn, +5% YoY on a like-for-like basis, hit by a heatwave that cost operating days (some impact spilled into Q2). £266 / 280 / 294 mn (+5% a year) at ₹127/£: FY27E is the first full year.
segments._marginWhy: Post-IFRS 16 EBITDA after new-centre (Birmingham) losses: 8.6% (Q3FY26 stub), 10.5% (Q4FY26), 8.8% (Q1FY27; pre-IFRS 5.1%). Levers: procurement, NH's software (certification delayed 4-6 months), more private/self-pay patients (a 4-5 year journey from ~95% NHS; the nearest peer is ~70% NHS). Management: UK margins will move toward local peers, not India/Cayman levels. 9.5% / 11% / 12%.

segments.name: Cayman insurance (CIHL)
segments._why: Cayman Integrated Healthcare Ltd, selling policies since Jan-2025: revenue US$3.6 mn (FY25), US$41.8 mn (FY26), US$15.4 mn in Q1FY27; book ~US$60 mn annualised. New client additions are being slowed after a 110-112% loss ratio. US$64 / 68 / 71 mn at ₹94.7.
segments._marginWhy: EBITDA US$-8.0 mn in FY26 (Q4 US$-5.1 mn), US$-3.7 mn in Q1FY27. July-2026 renewals (about a third of accounts) repriced with 100% retention; January renewals next; management says the worst is behind it barring large claims; Kotak expects breakeven by end-FY28. US$-8.0 / -2.0 / +1.5 mn (-12.5% / -2.9% / +2.1%).

segments.name: India clinics & insurance (NHIC + NHIL)
segments._why: Clinics (NHIC: 11 clinics in Bengaluru and Hosur, revenue ₹60.9 cr in FY26, ₹17.1 cr in Q1FY27, +26%) plus Narayana Health Insurance (NHIL: GWP ₹43.8 cr in FY26, ₹26.2 cr in Q1FY27; net earned premium ₹10.1 cr in Q1FY27; FY26 revenue ~₹16.8 cr = AR insurance segment less CIHL). Clinics to double over time (Kolkata in FY27): clinics ₹78 / 95 / 110 cr, NHIL earned premium ₹50 / 90 / 140 cr.
segments._marginWhy: Reported only together: EBITDA ₹-32.4 cr (FY24), ₹-64.5 cr (FY25), ₹-67.2 cr (FY26), ₹-32.8 cr in Q1FY27 alone (clinics ~₹-15 cr; NHIL claims ratio 219% on a small book). Management: clinic cash burn continues at a similar run rate; insurance losses volatile until the book scales. Kotak expects ₹-120 cr in FY27E. We use ₹-120 / -95 / -70 cr.

segments.name: Eliminations & other
segments._why: Consolidated revenue less the segments (inter-company sales between insurers, clinics and hospitals, software subsidiaries): ₹-23 cr (FY25), ₹-40 cr (FY26), ₹-6 cr in Q1FY27. ₹-25 / -27 / -30 cr.
segments._marginWhy: Zero margin (engine workaround: no elimination line).

assumptions._unallocLabel: Unallocated: one-time acquisition costs and Screener reclassification
assumptions._unallocWhy: Sum of segment EBITDA less Screener EBITDA: ₹56 cr in FY26 = the ₹76 cr one-time PPG acquisition cost less ~₹24 cr that Screener moves from finance cost into EBITDA, less rounding. Zero in Q1FY27 (Screener ₹468 cr = company ₹470 cr = sum of PL's segments). Zero in forecasts.

businessLines._why: Revenue build behind the segments; NH.ctx.js checks that it sums to model revenue. India: occupied beds = revenue ÷ ARPOB (the company reports ARPOB as ₹ mn per occupied bed a year and does not report occupancy; it says it 'typically operates between 60% and 65%' on its census basis). Occupied beds were ~2,774 (FY24), ~2,708 (FY25), ~2,648 (FY26) and ~2,712 in Q1FY27 on ~5,450 operational beds (~50% of operational beds): ARPOB did the work. Operational beds: 5,451 (Mar-26), 5,461 (Jun-26); +100 South-West Bengaluru (end-Q2FY27), +515 HSR and Raipur (FY28, weighted ~150 in FY28E and ~515 in FY29E). FX held at the Q1FY27 averages implied by the deck and PL's rupee figures (₹94.7/US$, ₹127/GBP; FY26 averages ~₹88.3 and ~₹118).

assumptions._capexWhy: India: FY27 plan ₹460 cr greenfield + ₹270 cr replacement/maintenance (Q1FY27 actual ₹74.5 cr + ₹31.4 cr); the six projects (2,035 beds for ₹2,974 cr: HSR 215 beds ₹490 cr FY28, Raipur 300 beds ₹540 cr FY28, Rajarhat 350 beds ₹900 cr FY29, Central Bengaluru 220 beds ₹160 cr FY29, South Bengaluru 350 beds ₹800 cr FY30, South-West Bengaluru 100 beds ₹84 cr FY27) need ~₹2,700 cr more; management said ~₹1,000 cr a year in FY28-29 (Q4FY26 call). Plus UK and Cayman maintenance (~₹80-100 cr; no Cayman expansion planned) and new leases (~₹100-130 cr a year; the model counts leases as debt, so new leases are added to capex). ₹950 / 1,350 / 1,300 cr. The engine depreciates capex at once while it sits in CWIP, which overstates FY28-29E depreciation slightly.
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 D&A ₹448 cr with five months of UK (incl. right-of-use ₹79 cr and intangibles ₹70 cr, of which PPG purchase-price amortisation ~£2.3 mn); Q1FY27 ₹156 cr (₹624 cr annualised) with a full UK quarter = ~6.1% of average gross block. FY27E ~₹627 cr.
assumptions._treasuryWhy: Zero: the engine applies the yield to net cash, and NH has net debt (₹3,156 cr incl. ₹991 cr of leases at Mar-26). Treasury income is built on gross cash in otherIncome.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Built from AR FY26 note 24 (₹100.2 cr): (1) treasury = deposit interest ₹29.4 cr + interest on amortised-cost assets ₹19.0 cr + mutual-fund gains ₹18.4 cr = ₹66.8 cr on ~₹2,200 cr average cash and investments (cash rose late in the year); Q1FY27 ~₹27.5 cr on ~₹2,760 cr = ~4.0%. We take 4.0% on average gross cash of ₹2,500 / 2,100 / 1,800 cr as capex draws it down = ₹100 / 84 / 72 cr. (2) Recurring non-treasury: other interest ₹11.0 cr, grant income ₹7.3 cr (non-cash), miscellaneous ₹13.8 cr: ₹28 / 29 / 30 cr. (3) Share of associate/JV losses (Reya Health, Everhope JV): ₹-5.6 cr in FY26, ₹-1.9 cr in Q1FY27: ₹-8 cr a year. Left out: write-backs ₹1.2 cr. FY27E ₹120 cr vs company FY26 ₹100.2 cr and the twelve months to Jun-26 ~₹112 cr (company). Screener's FY26 ₹37 cr and TTM ₹55 cr are lower because Screener nets the ₹51 cr labour-code exceptional and the associate loss into other income.
assumptions._interestWhy: FY26 ₹243.7 cr (term loans ₹122.9 cr, NCDs ₹66.8 cr, leases ₹40.1 cr, other ₹14.0 cr; Screener ₹266 cr); Q1FY27 ₹86.8 cr (₹347 cr annualised) with a full quarter of the £150 mn PPG acquisition loan and UK leases. Borrowings ₹4,878 cr at Jun-26 (US$115 mn and £150 mn foreign-currency). Net debt rises for 2-3 years as the ₹3,000 cr India programme is part debt-funded (management: back below today's levels by FY30), while the UK loan amortises from UK cash flow over seven years: ₹345 / 365 / 375 cr.
assumptions._taxWhy: Effective tax 15.4% (FY25), 16.3% (FY26, incl. a deferred-tax credit), 20.4% (Q1FY27). Cayman profits are not taxed locally; India and the UK pay ~25%. As India's share of profit rises, 18.5% / 19% / 19.5%. Minorities (Meridian Medical, Shepton Mallet JV) are ~₹0.4 cr a year: ignored.
assumptions._payoutWhy: Dividend ~10-12% of profit (₹91 cr paid in FY26, ₹4.5 a share); capex absorbs the rest.

dcf._betaWhy: The engine discounts at one rate. Net debt incl. leases ~₹3,000-3,600 cr against ~₹36,600 cr of market value (~9% of EV): cost of equity ~12.1% (beta 0.93) on ~91% and post-tax cost of debt ~5.6% on ~9% gives a WACC of ~11.6%, which is what beta 0.85 produces (6.5% + 0.85 × 6%).
dcf._tgWhy: India hospitals can grow 8-10% nominal for a long time, but Cayman is a small island market and the UK is NHS-priced: a blended 5.5%.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades from ~9% (FY29E) to 7% by year 15 as the India bed programme matures and the overseas businesses grow at mid-single digits.
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: 21% post-Ind AS: India ~23-24% less start-up losses, Cayman ~44% on a shrinking share, UK low-teens, insurance at breakeven.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex (incl. new leases) falls from ~10-11% of revenue in FY28-29E to 6.5%: maintenance (~3%) plus growth beds; depreciation ~5.5% of revenue.

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: India hospitals keep compounding ARPOB at ~9% with volumes rising as new beds open on time, Cayman insurance breaks even in FY28 and steers more patients to the hospital, and the UK reaches ~13-14% margins on a richer private mix.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: India ARPOB growth slows to price increases only while HSR, Raipur and Rajarhat slip and carry start-up losses, Cayman growth stalls and insurance keeps losing money, and the UK stays near 8% margins with NHS tariff pressure.

parts.name: India hospitals
parts.metricLabel: Sep-28E EBITDA (half FY28E + half FY29E) x EV/EBITDA
parts.note: Derived: NH's own one-year-forward EV/EBITDA since Apr-2021 has a median of 16.4x (no trough years; leases in EV, post-Ind AS EBITDA; points before the Nov-2025 UK deal use forward EBITDA without the UK). Listed hospital peers traded a median 12.3% below their five-year EV/EBITDA medians on 30-Sep-2026 (Apollo, Max, Fortis, Medanta, Rainbow, Jupiter; KIMS and Aster left out), so the India + Cayman business is worth ~14.4x. Cayman's EBITDA grows ~8.6% a year in FY26-29E against India's ~14.4%, so we value Cayman at 0.6x the India multiple (the street uses 0.60-0.67x). On the FY25-26 mix (India 60%, Cayman 40% of the two businesses' EBITDA) that solves to India 17.1x → 17x and Cayman 10.3x → 10.5x. Street: PL 25x, ICICI Direct 24x on FY28E. Bull 22x / bear 15.5x = the 75th / 25th percentile of the history (18.7x / 12.9x) on the same split.

parts.metricLabel: PV at Sep-2027 of losses still to come (H2FY28E onward), breakeven FY32E (bull FY31E, bear FY33E), at a 12.1% cost of equity

methods.name: Sum of the parts
methods.why: How the street values Narayana: every disclosed method is a sum of the parts on EV/EBITDA (PL: India 25x, international 15x on FY28E; ICICI Direct: India 24x, Cayman 16x, UK 4x; Kotak's summary cites ~17x pre-Ind AS for India). The businesses differ in growth, currency, tax and risk, so we value India hospitals, Cayman hospitals and the UK on Sep-28E EBITDA (post-Ind AS), deduct the present value of the start-up losses of the India clinics + insurer and the Cayman insurer until breakeven, less net debt including lease liabilities at Sep-27E. Multiples are derived from NH's own forward EV/EBITDA history and the sector de-rating, not taken from the street.

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: Cross-check on earnings: NH's one-year-forward P/E since Apr-2021 has a median of 30.1x (forwardMedian; no trough years), cut by the 13.4% median P/E de-rating of the same six peers = 26.1x → 26x on Sep-28E EPS. Bull 33x (75th percentile, 33.3x), bear 23x (scaled with the EV/EBITDA anchor).

methods.name: DCF
methods.why: Tests whether cash flows support the price: 15-year FCFF (capex incl. new leases), discount rate 11.6% (beta set so the single rate equals WACC), terminal growth 5.5%, less net debt incl. leases at Mar-27E.

lossPV._why: Start-up losses are valued at the present value of the losses still to come until breakeven, not as a perpetuity (a negative EBITDA × a multiple assumes they never end). PV at the Sep-2027 target date of: half of FY28E, FY29E, then a straight-line run-off to zero in the breakeven year; pre-tax EBITDA losses; discounted at our 12.1% cost of equity (6.5% + 0.93 × 6%, see dcf._betaWhy). Losses before the target date are already in net debt at Sep-27E. The insurers' capital (AR FY26 note 33: insurance segment capital employed ₹170 cr at Mar-26; NH's equity investment in NHIL ₹122 cr) sits in consolidated cash and investments and so already reduces our net debt; we do not add it again. Cayman insurance's profits after breakeven are not valued separately: they show up as patient steerage in Cayman hospital EBITDA (management asks that Cayman be judged as one business).

ic._why: No sourced breakeven date: management says clinics break even ~18 months after opening and current losses are mostly integrated-care overheads, but cash burn continues at a similar rate in FY27 while the clinic count doubles; for NHIL it 'can't give a date'. Neither unit is described as structurally loss-making (clinics are being folded into the hospitals, overheads shared with the parent; NHIL is scaling toward retail/SME with solvency of 167%), so no perpetuity charge is kept. Base: our ₹-120 / -95 / -70 cr path (FY27-29E) runs off to zero by FY32E; bull (losses shrink faster) FY31E; bear FY33E.

cihl._why: Kotak expects CIHL breakeven by end-FY28E; management says losses have bottomed and repricing (July and January renewals) improves profitability over 2-3 quarters. Our base has US$-2.0 mn in FY28E and +US$1.5 mn in FY29E (breakeven in FY29E); bull FY28E; bear FY30E.

valuation._roundWhy: Target rounded to ₹5, not ₹10: the base and bear SOTP values (₹1,684.99 and ₹1,244.99) sit on the ₹10 rounding boundary, where the Excel model's own recalculation (₹1,685.0 and ₹1,245.0) would round the other way. Presentation only; the valuation is unchanged.

cover.headline: An excellent Indian hospital business inside a costlier, slower group: at ₹1,791 the market already pays the full price
cover.lead: Narayana Health runs India's lowest-cost large hospital network (5,461 operational beds; existing beds cost ~₹75 lakh each), a US-dollar hospital business in the Cayman Islands, and since Nov-2025 the UK's Practice Plus Group; it also funds two young insurers and a clinic chain. The India hospitals are the jewel: EBITDA +40% in Q1FY27 with no new beds, margin 24.8%. The rest of the group dilutes them: the UK earns ~9% on NHS work, and the insurers and clinics lost ₹139 cr in FY26 and ₹68 cr in Q1FY27 alone. The street values NH on a **sum of the parts on EV/EBITDA** (India 24-25x, Cayman/international 15-16x, FY28E). We forecast EBITDA of ₹2,152 / 2,504 / 2,803 cr and EPS of ₹51.8 / 61.3 / 68.6 for FY27-29E, 15% below PL for FY28E. Valuing India at **17x**, Cayman at **10.5x** and the UK at **7x** (at cost) on Sep-28E EBITDA, multiples derived from NH's own 16.4x forward EV/EBITDA history and the sector's 12% de-rating, and deducting the present value of the insurance and clinic losses until breakeven (₹172 cr), gives **{{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}})**: **we initiate with SELL.** Cross-checks: P/E ₹1,688, DCF ₹1,323. Bull case {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear case {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}.

arguments.h: India: best-in-class cost, growth bought with price
arguments.p: India hospital ARPOB rose from ₹14.0 mn (FY24) to ₹19.2 mn (Q1FY27) a year per occupied bed, and the margin from 19.9% to 24.8%. But occupied beds fell ~5% over FY24-26 (to ~2,650 on ~5,450 beds), and the next 2,035 beds cost ₹1.8-2.6 cr each, three times the old ones. We model India revenue +{{as.segments.0.growth.0|pct}} / +{{as.segments.0.growth.1|pct}} / +{{as.segments.0.growth.2|pct}}.

Cayman (~44% margin on PL's split) is slowing to single-digit growth; the UK (~9%, ~95% NHS-funded, £150 mn acquisition loan) is a turnaround bet with a heatwave-hit first full quarter; Cayman insurance lost US$3.7 mn and India clinics + insurance ₹33 cr in Q1FY27. Group EBITDA margin {{F.ebitdaMargin.0|pct}} in FY27E vs India's ~24%.

Our FY28E EPS of ₹61.3 is 15% below PL (₹72.1) and 17% below ICICI Direct (₹73.8): we keep depreciation and interest at the Q1FY27 run-rate, give the UK and Cayman insurer a slower turnaround, and assume clinic and India insurance losses of ₹120 cr in FY27E (as Kotak does).

arguments.h: Valuation: full on its own history
arguments.p: At ₹1,791 NH trades at 15.9x our FY28E EV/EBITDA, right at its 16.4x forward median since Apr-2021, while listed hospitals had de-rated ~12%. Valuing Cayman and the UK at our multiples, today's price already pays ~19.2x for India. The DCF (₹1,323) also says the price is ahead of the cash flows.

sections.title: Four businesses under one brand: India hospitals, a Cayman hospital and insurer, a UK NHS provider, and Indian clinics and insurance

blocks.p: **India hospitals** (₹4,740 cr revenue in FY26, 60% of the group): 20 hospitals and heart centres with 5,461 operational beds (5,775 capacity) in six clusters, led by Bengaluru (37% of India hospital revenue) and Kolkata (25%). About three-quarters of revenue comes from hospitals Narayana owns; a quarter from hospitals it runs for trusts and state governments on rental or revenue-share terms (Raipur, Jamshedpur, Mumbai and others), which is part of why its beds are so cheap. Cardiac sciences are a third of revenue, oncology 16%. The model is high volume at low prices: 2,137 cardiac surgeries at the Bengaluru flagship in Q1FY27 and ~100 robotic cardiac cases a month, at an ARPOB of ~₹52,600 a day, below most listed peers.

**Cayman Islands** (₹1,889 cr, 24%): Health City Cayman Islands and Health City Camana Bay, 164 beds, earning US dollars (hospital revenue US$178.7 mn in FY26, +27%) with no local corporate tax, plus an insurer (CIHL) that started selling in Jan-2025 and steers members to the hospitals (US$41.8 mn revenue, US$-8 mn EBITDA in FY26). **United Kingdom** (₹1,299 cr in five months; ~₹3,400 cr a year): Practice Plus Group Hospitals, bought in Nov-2025: 13 facilities, 330 beds, 37 theatres, day-care orthopaedics, ophthalmology and diagnostics, ~95% paid by the NHS. **India integrated care**: 11 clinics in Bengaluru and Hosur (₹61 cr revenue) and Narayana Health Insurance (₹44 cr of premium written); together they lost ₹67 cr in FY26.

blocks.p: Indian private hospitals are in a bed-building cycle financed by strong cash flows, while price (ARPOB) rather than volume has driven growth for the established chains. blocks.p: On 30-Oct-2025 Narayana's UK subsidiary agreed to buy Practice Plus Group Hospitals from Bridgepoint-owned Practice Plus Group for £188.8 mn (₹2,201 cr), completing on 6-Nov-2025. The EV of ~£183 mn was 9.2x FY25 EBITDA before IFRS 16 (£20 mn) and 7-8x the next twelve months; after IFRS 16 FY25 EBITDA was £29 mn, both excluding £6.1 mn of start-up losses at the new Birmingham centre. A £150 mn seven-year loan sits in the UK business and is to be repaid from its cash flow. PPG grew revenue 12% a year for five years (£229 mn in FY24, £250 mn FY25E, September year-ends); it is the UK's fifth-largest private network and fourth-largest NHS provider, but ~95% of revenue is NHS-funded (Spire ~35%, Ramsay 60-70%).

A severe heatwave knocked out chillers and theatre days, and some impact spilled into Q2. Separation from the seller is complete; certification of NH's software as a medical device adds 4-6 months.

**The plan:** standardise implants and consumables, automate administration (NH's Athma software), and raise the private (self-pay and insured) share from ~5-7% toward the ~30% of the nearest peer over 4-5 years. sections.title: Insurance and clinics: a sound idea that costs ₹100-150 cr a year until it works

blocks.p: Narayana is trying to become a "payer-provider": own the patient through clinics and an insurance policy, then treat them in its hospitals, as Kaiser Permanente does in the US. It runs this experiment in two places. In the Cayman Islands CIHL already insures a large share of the market and lifts hospital volumes. In India, 11 clinics (₹61 cr revenue, ~30% of Bengaluru hospital outpatient footfall) and Narayana Health Insurance (premium ₹44 cr in FY26, ₹26 cr in Q1FY27) are small. Management says it is the only hospital-promoted insurer in India and that it can price group renewals using its own clinical data, but Indian rules do not let it reprice individuals for deteriorating health.

blocks.callout: **Honest verdict:** Narayana's moat is cost and clinical volume in Indian tertiary care, built over 25 years on cheap beds and high throughput. It is a genuine advantage, but it is narrowing as the company builds beds at today's prices and pays to enter new businesses. Cayman is a good niche business with a small market. The UK has no moat today: Narayana is a price-taker from a single buyer (the NHS) and must prove it can run a lower-cost hospital in a high-cost country.

sections.title: Revenue tripled since FY20, but the jump in FY26 was bought: the UK added 16% of revenue at a 10% margin

blocks.p: Narayana's revenue grew from ₹3,128 cr in FY20 to ₹7,896 cr in FY26 (17% a year). Strip out the two step-changes and the organic story is steadier: FY21 fell 17% in the Covid lockdowns; FY22-25 grew 43%, 22%, 8% and 12% as India recovered and the Cayman Islands business doubled; FY26 grew 44% because the UK's Practice Plus Group (PPG) was consolidated from 6-Nov-2025 (₹1,299 cr in five months) and Cayman grew 60% in rupees (new Camana Bay hospital plus its own insurer). Without the UK, revenue grew ~20%. Profit tells a less flattering story: net profit was ₹790 cr in FY24, ₹791 cr in FY25 and ₹806 cr in FY26, flat for three years, because interest, depreciation and the losses of new businesses (clinics, two insurers) absorbed the EBITDA growth.

sections.title: From no new beds to ₹3,000 cr of new hospitals and a UK buyout: returns fall before they can rise

blocks.p: For a decade Narayana grew without adding beds in India; management says it is "the only listed group that has not added a single bed from the time of listing". Its spending went to Cayman (Camana Bay), refurbishment and technology. That has changed. In FY26 it bought the UK's Practice Plus Group for ₹2,201 cr (£188.8 mn), financed with a £150 mn seven-year loan housed in the UK business, and it has committed ~₹3,000 cr to six India projects (2,035 beds) to be completed in FY27-FY30. ROCE (Screener) fell from 32% (FY23) to 16% (FY26); management itself says it is "diluting ROCE for growth".

sections.title: Earnings quality: cash-generative, but four businesses, two EBITDA definitions and an acquisition make the numbers hard to read

bullets: **Which EBITDA?** Narayana's own "EBITDA" includes other income (FY26 ₹1,717 cr; adjusted for one-time UK costs ₹1,793 cr). Screener's (and our model's) excludes it: ₹1,641 cr in FY26, which still contains the ₹76 cr one-time acquisition cost and ~₹24 cr moved from finance cost. Brokers mostly use the company's ex-other-income figure (PL FY26 ₹1,693 cr).

**Segment opacity.** The company reports India hospital EBITDA but not Cayman ("it is possible for you to work that number"). The India figure includes ~₹66-79 cr a year of income that is eliminated on consolidation, so India looks better and Cayman worse than PL's split; we use PL's split, which adds up.

**Ind AS 116.** Lease liabilities rose to ₹991 cr (₹708 cr from PPG). Rent of ~₹160 cr a year is therefore below EBITDA (depreciation and interest): pre-Ind AS margin ~{{F.ebitdaMargin.0|pct}} less ~1.5pp. In the UK the gap is ~£2.4 mn a quarter (post- vs pre-IFRS 16 EBITDA).

**Purchase accounting.** Of the ₹2,201 cr PPG price, ₹1,181 cr is goodwill and ₹883 cr customer and brand intangibles (amortised; ~£2.3 mn in five months). Amortisation and acquisition interest turned a £2.7 mn UK hospital profit into a £1.9 mn loss in FY26.

**One-offs in FY26:** ₹51 cr labour-code charge (exceptional), ₹76 cr UK acquisition costs (in other expenses), ₹6.2 cr Jammu write-down (discontinued). Q4FY26 reclassified Cayman doctor fees between cost lines (professional fees looked negative that quarter).
**Cash conversion.** Operating cash flow was 99% of EBITDA in FY26 (76% in FY25); suppliers fund working capital (payable days ~250). Government scheme receivables are slow (AR FY26).
**Tax.** 15-16% effective in FY25-26 because Cayman profits are untaxed locally; 20.4% in Q1FY27. A Cayman tax regime change or dividend withholding would raise it.
**Audit.** Deloitte Haskins & Sells LLP; unqualified opinion.

blocks.callout: **Accounting flag: AMBER.** Nothing suggests aggressive accounting, and cash generation is real. But the reported numbers mix four businesses, two EBITDA definitions, purchase accounting and frequent reclassifications, and the company declines to report Cayman profit. Investors should rebuild the segments (as we do) rather than read the headline margin.

Against this the group held ₹2,129 cr of cash and bank balances and ₹573 cr of investments. The company reports net debt (excluding leases) of ₹2,240 cr at Mar-26 and ₹1,967 cr at Jun-26 (0.42x equity). Under Ind AS 116 it also carries ₹991 cr of lease liabilities (₹708 cr came with PPG), which Screener includes in borrowings. Our model uses that broader basis (post-Ind AS EBITDA with leases as debt): net debt ₹{{A.netDebt.11|num}} cr at Mar-26. ICRA rates the company AA (Stable).

blocks.p: Every broker method we could see is a **sum of the parts on EV/EBITDA**, with India at 24-25x and Cayman/international at 15-16x on FY28E. We use the same method, applied to the EBITDA the market will look at in September 2027 (Sep-28E: half FY28E, half FY29E), with three differences. (1) Our EBITDA is post-Ind AS 116 and we count lease liabilities (₹991 cr) as debt; PL and ICICI use post-Ind AS EBITDA but leave leases out of debt, which flatters their targets by ~₹45-50 a share. (2) We deduct the present value of the start-up losses (India clinics + insurer, Cayman insurer) until breakeven, instead of capitalising a negative EBITDA at a multiple, which would assume the losses never end. (3) We derive the multiples from Narayana's own trading history and the sector de-rating rather than from where larger peers trade.

exhibit.title: Terms used in this report
head: Term
What it means
rows: Beds built vs beds staffed and open. Narayana: 6,269 capacity and 5,955 operational beds (Jun-2026), of which 5,461 operational in India.
Average revenue per occupied bed. Narayana reports it per year (₹19.2 mn in Q1FY27, ~₹52,600 a day): hospital revenue ÷ occupied beds.
Beds filled on an average day. Narayana does not report occupancy; we derive occupied beds as India hospital revenue ÷ ARPOB.
Average revenue per patient (inpatient or outpatient). Narayana prefers it to ARPOB.
Average length of stay of an inpatient (4.3 days in Q1FY27; target 3.9-4.0).
Inpatients (admitted; counted as discharges) and outpatients (consultations, day care).
Owned: Narayana owns the land and building. Operated: it runs a trust- or government-owned hospital on rental or revenue-share terms and keeps the P&L.
NH Integrated Care (clinics in Bengaluru and Hosur); Narayana Health Insurance (India); Cayman Integrated Healthcare (the Cayman insurer).
One group that both insures and treats the patient, so it gains when patients stay healthy and are treated efficiently.
GWP / NEP / claims ratio / combined ratio

Gross written premium (policies sold); net earned premium (the part of premium that belongs to the period, after reinsurance); claims ÷ NEP; claims plus expenses ÷ premium. Above 100% = underwriting loss.
The UK's state-funded National Health Service, which buys ~95% of PPG's care at set tariffs; private pay = self-pay patients and private medical insurance.

Earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation, with rent treated as a lease (interest + depreciation) rather than an expense. Pre-Ind AS (or pre-IFRS 16) EBITDA deducts rent. Narayana's own "EBITDA" also includes other income; ours does not.
The present value of future rent under long leases, shown as debt under Ind AS 116 (₹991 cr at Mar-2026). We count them in net debt because our EBITDA excludes rent.
Purchase-price allocation: on an acquisition, the price above the book value of assets is split into identifiable intangibles (amortised) and goodwill (not amortised, tested for impairment).
Valuing each business separately (here EV/EBITDA multiples on each segment's EBITDA) and adding them up, less net debt.
Enterprise value = market value of equity + net debt (incl. leases). EV/EBITDA = what investors pay per rupee of EBITDA.
Price (or EV) ÷ next full fiscal year's earnings (or EBITDA).
Half FY28E + half FY29E: the twelve months a buyer looks at in September 2027, when our 12-month target falls due.
A fall in the multiple investors pay; we measure it as the trailing multiple vs its own five-year median.
Return on capital employed (operating profit ÷ debt + equity); return on equity (net profit ÷ shareholders' equity).
Discounted cash flow: the present value of future free cash flows. WACC: the blended cost of equity and debt used to discount them.
The UK equivalent of pre-Ind AS 116: EBITDA after deducting rent. PPG FY25: £20 mn pre-IFRS 16, £29 mn post.

segments._why: Cayman Integrated Healthcare Ltd, selling policies since Jan-2025: revenue US$3.6 mn (FY25), US$41.8 mn (FY26), US$15.4 mn in Q1FY27; book ~US$60 mn annualised. New client additions are being slowed after a 110-112% loss ratio. US$64 / 68 / 71 mn at ₹94.7.
segments._marginWhy: EBITDA US$-8.0 mn in FY26 (Q4 US$-5.1 mn), US$-3.7 mn in Q1FY27. July-2026 renewals (about a third of accounts) repriced with 100% retention; January renewals next; management says the worst is behind it barring large claims; Kotak expects breakeven by end-FY28. US$-8.0 / -2.0 / +1.5 mn (-12.5% / -2.9% / +2.1%).

segments.name: India clinics & insurance (NHIC + NHIL)
segments._why: Clinics (NHIC: 11 clinics in Bengaluru and Hosur, revenue ₹60.9 cr in FY26, ₹17.1 cr in Q1FY27, +26%) plus Narayana Health Insurance (NHIL: GWP ₹43.8 cr in FY26, ₹26.2 cr in Q1FY27; net earned premium ₹10.1 cr in Q1FY27; FY26 revenue ~₹16.8 cr = AR insurance segment less CIHL). Clinics to double over time (Kolkata in FY27): clinics ₹78 / 95 / 110 cr, NHIL earned premium ₹50 / 90 / 140 cr.

assumptions._unallocLabel: Unallocated: one-time acquisition costs and Screener reclassification
assumptions._unallocWhy: Sum of segment EBITDA less Screener EBITDA: ₹56 cr in FY26 = the ₹76 cr one-time PPG acquisition cost less ~₹24 cr that Screener moves from finance cost into EBITDA, less rounding. Zero in Q1FY27 (Screener ₹468 cr = company ₹470 cr = sum of PL's segments). Zero in forecasts.

businessLines._why: Revenue build behind the segments; NH.ctx.js checks that it sums to model revenue. India: occupied beds = revenue ÷ ARPOB (the company reports ARPOB as ₹ mn per occupied bed a year and does not report occupancy; it says it 'typically operates between 60% and 65%' on its census basis). Occupied beds were ~2,774 (FY24), ~2,708 (FY25), ~2,648 (FY26) and ~2,712 in Q1FY27 on ~5,450 operational beds (~50% of operational beds): ARPOB did the work. Operational beds: 5,451 (Mar-26), 5,461 (Jun-26); +100 South-West Bengaluru (end-Q2FY27), +515 HSR and Raipur (FY28, weighted ~150 in FY28E and ~515 in FY29E). FX held at the Q1FY27 averages implied by the deck and PL's rupee figures (₹94.7/US$, ₹127/GBP; FY26 averages ~₹88.3 and ~₹118).

assumptions._capexWhy: India: FY27 plan ₹460 cr greenfield + ₹270 cr replacement/maintenance (Q1FY27 actual ₹74.5 cr + ₹31.4 cr); the six projects (2,035 beds for ₹2,974 cr: HSR 215 beds ₹490 cr FY28, Raipur 300 beds ₹540 cr FY28, Rajarhat 350 beds ₹900 cr FY29, Central Bengaluru 220 beds ₹160 cr FY29, South Bengaluru 350 beds ₹800 cr FY30, South-West Bengaluru 100 beds ₹84 cr FY27) need ~₹2,700 cr more; management said ~₹1,000 cr a year in FY28-29 (Q4FY26 call). assumptions._depWhy: FY26 D&A ₹448 cr with five months of UK (incl. right-of-use ₹79 cr and intangibles ₹70 cr, of which PPG purchase-price amortisation ~£2.3 mn); Q1FY27 ₹156 cr (₹624 cr annualised) with a full UK quarter = ~6.1% of average gross block. FY27E ~₹627 cr.
assumptions._treasuryWhy: Zero: the engine applies the yield to net cash, and NH has net debt (₹3,156 cr incl. ₹991 cr of leases at Mar-26). Treasury income is built on gross cash in otherIncome.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Built from AR FY26 note 24 (₹100.2 cr): (1) treasury = deposit interest ₹29.4 cr + interest on amortised-cost assets ₹19.0 cr + mutual-fund gains ₹18.4 cr = ₹66.8 cr on ~₹2,200 cr average cash and investments (cash rose late in the year); Q1FY27 ~₹27.5 cr on ~₹2,760 cr = ~4.0%. FY27E ₹120 cr vs company FY26 ₹100.2 cr and the twelve months to Jun-26 ~₹112 cr (company). Screener's FY26 ₹37 cr and TTM ₹55 cr are lower because Screener nets the ₹51 cr labour-code exceptional and the associate loss into other income.
assumptions._interestWhy: FY26 ₹243.7 cr (term loans ₹122.9 cr, NCDs ₹66.8 cr, leases ₹40.1 cr, other ₹14.0 cr; Screener ₹266 cr); Q1FY27 ₹86.8 cr (₹347 cr annualised) with a full quarter of the £150 mn PPG acquisition loan and UK leases. assumptions._taxWhy: Effective tax 15.4% (FY25), 16.3% (FY26, incl. a deferred-tax credit), 20.4% (Q1FY27). Cayman profits are not taxed locally; India and the UK pay ~25%. As India's share of profit rises, 18.5% / 19% / 19.5%. Minorities (Meridian Medical, Shepton Mallet JV) are ~₹0.4 cr a year: ignored.
assumptions._payoutWhy: Dividend ~10-12% of profit (₹91 cr paid in FY26, ₹4.5 a share); capex absorbs the rest.

dcf._betaWhy: The engine discounts at one rate. Net debt incl. leases ~₹3,000-3,600 cr against ~₹36,600 cr of market value (~9% of EV): cost of equity ~12.1% (beta 0.93) on ~91% and post-tax cost of debt ~5.6% on ~9% gives a WACC of ~11.6%, which is what beta 0.85 produces (6.5% + 0.85 × 6%).
dcf._tgWhy: India hospitals can grow 8-10% nominal for a long time, but Cayman is a small island market and the UK is NHS-priced: a blended 5.5%.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades from ~9% (FY29E) to 7% by year 15 as the India bed programme matures and the overseas businesses grow at mid-single digits.
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: 21% post-Ind AS: India ~23-24% less start-up losses, Cayman ~44% on a shrinking share, UK low-teens, insurance at breakeven.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex (incl. new leases) falls from ~10-11% of revenue in FY28-29E to 6.5%: maintenance (~3%) plus growth beds; depreciation ~5.5% of revenue.

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: India hospitals keep compounding ARPOB at ~9% with volumes rising as new beds open on time, Cayman insurance breaks even in FY28 and steers more patients to the hospital, and the UK reaches ~13-14% margins on a richer private mix.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: India ARPOB growth slows to price increases only while HSR, Raipur and Rajarhat slip and carry start-up losses, Cayman growth stalls and insurance keeps losing money, and the UK stays near 8% margins with NHS tariff pressure.

parts.name: India hospitals
parts.metricLabel: Sep-28E EBITDA (half FY28E + half FY29E) x EV/EBITDA
parts.note: Derived: NH's own one-year-forward EV/EBITDA since Apr-2021 has a median of 16.4x (no trough years; leases in EV, post-Ind AS EBITDA; points before the Nov-2025 UK deal use forward EBITDA without the UK). Listed hospital peers traded a median 12.3% below their five-year EV/EBITDA medians on 30-Sep-2026 (Apollo, Max, Fortis, Medanta, Rainbow, Jupiter; KIMS and Aster left out), so the India + Cayman business is worth ~14.4x. Cayman's EBITDA grows ~8.6% a year in FY26-29E against India's ~14.4%, so we value Cayman at 0.6x the India multiple (the street uses 0.60-0.67x). On the FY25-26 mix (India 60%, Cayman 40% of the two businesses' EBITDA) that solves to India 17.1x → 17x and Cayman 10.3x → 10.5x. Street: PL 25x, ICICI Direct 24x on FY28E. Bull 22x / bear 15.5x = the 75th / 25th percentile of the history (18.7x / 12.9x) on the same split.

parts.name: Less: India clinics & insurance, PV of losses to breakeven
parts.metricLabel: PV at Sep-2027 of losses still to come (H2FY28E onward), breakeven FY32E (bull FY31E, bear FY33E), at a 12.1% cost of equity
parts.note: Present value of the forecast losses until breakeven, not a perpetuity: NHIC clinics + NHIL lose ₹120 / 95 / 70 cr in FY27-29E on our numbers and run off to zero by FY32E. Losses before the target date are in net debt; NHIL's capital is in consolidated cash (not added again).

parts.name: Cayman hospitals
parts.note: 0.6x the India multiple (relative EBITDA growth FY26-29E: Cayman hospitals ~8.6% a year vs India ~14.4%); PL 15x 'international', ICICI Direct 16x. US-dollar, untaxed locally, but one island and slowing growth. Bull 13.5x, bear 9x.

parts.name: Less: Cayman insurance, PV of losses to breakeven
parts.metricLabel: PV at Sep-2027 of losses still to come, breakeven FY29E (bull FY28E, bear FY30E), at a 12.1% cost of equity
parts.note: Present value of CIHL's remaining losses (half of FY28E's US$-2.0 mn) until breakeven in FY29E; later profits are captured in Cayman hospital volumes. Its capital is in consolidated cash.

parts.name: UK (Practice Plus Group)
parts.note: At cost: NH paid ₹2,201 cr (£188.8 mn) and took on ₹708 cr of leases, ~₹2,860 cr of EV after ₹46 cr of acquired cash; 7x our Sep-28E post-IFRS 16 EBITDA (~₹420 cr) returns roughly that. parts.name: Less: net debt incl. leases at Sep-27E
parts.metricLabel: Net debt at the target date (half Mar-27E + half Mar-28E)
parts.note: Model forecast: borrowings incl. lease liabilities less cash and investments, half Mar-27E + half Mar-28E (the 12-month target date).

methods.name: Sum of the parts
methods.why: How the street values Narayana: every disclosed method is a sum of the parts on EV/EBITDA (PL: India 25x, international 15x on FY28E; ICICI Direct: India 24x, Cayman 16x, UK 4x; Kotak's summary cites ~17x pre-Ind AS for India). The businesses differ in growth, currency, tax and risk, so we value India hospitals, Cayman hospitals and the UK on Sep-28E EBITDA (post-Ind AS), deduct the present value of the start-up losses of the India clinics + insurer and the Cayman insurer until breakeven, less net debt including lease liabilities at Sep-27E. Multiples are derived from NH's own forward EV/EBITDA history and the sector de-rating, not taken from the street.

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: Cross-check on earnings: NH's one-year-forward P/E since Apr-2021 has a median of 30.1x (forwardMedian; no trough years), cut by the 13.4% median P/E de-rating of the same six peers = 26.1x → 26x on Sep-28E EPS. Bull 33x (75th percentile, 33.3x), bear 23x (scaled with the EV/EBITDA anchor).

methods.name: DCF
methods.why: Tests whether cash flows support the price: 15-year FCFF (capex incl. new leases), discount rate 11.6% (beta set so the single rate equals WACC), terminal growth 5.5%, less net debt incl. leases at Mar-27E.

lossPV._why: Start-up losses are valued at the present value of the losses still to come until breakeven, not as a perpetuity (a negative EBITDA × a multiple assumes they never end). PV at the Sep-2027 target date of: half of FY28E, FY29E, then a straight-line run-off to zero in the breakeven year; pre-tax EBITDA losses; discounted at our 12.1% cost of equity (6.5% + 0.93 × 6%, see dcf._betaWhy). Losses before the target date are already in net debt at Sep-27E. The insurers' capital (AR FY26 note 33: insurance segment capital employed ₹170 cr at Mar-26; NH's equity investment in NHIL ₹122 cr) sits in consolidated cash and investments and so already reduces our net debt; we do not add it again. Cayman insurance's profits after breakeven are not valued separately: they show up as patient steerage in Cayman hospital EBITDA (management asks that Cayman be judged as one business).

ic._why: No sourced breakeven date: management says clinics break even ~18 months after opening and current losses are mostly integrated-care overheads, but cash burn continues at a similar rate in FY27 while the clinic count doubles; for NHIL it 'can't give a date'. Neither unit is described as structurally loss-making (clinics are being folded into the hospitals, overheads shared with the parent; NHIL is scaling toward retail/SME with solvency of 167%), so no perpetuity charge is kept. Base: our ₹-120 / -95 / -70 cr path (FY27-29E) runs off to zero by FY32E; bull (losses shrink faster) FY31E; bear FY33E.

cihl._why: Kotak expects CIHL breakeven by end-FY28E; management says losses have bottomed and repricing (July and January renewals) improves profitability over 2-3 quarters. Our base has US$-2.0 mn in FY28E and +US$1.5 mn in FY29E (breakeven in FY29E); bull FY28E; bear FY30E.

valuation._roundWhy: Target rounded to ₹5, not ₹10: the base and bear SOTP values (₹1,684.99 and ₹1,244.99) sit on the ₹10 rounding boundary, where the Excel model's own recalculation (₹1,685.0 and ₹1,245.0) would round the other way. Presentation only; the valuation is unchanged.
